title: What If Nobody Had Another Baby? Civilization Fails Before the Last Human

scenes.text: What if nobody on Earth had another baby? Civilization would collapse long before the last human.
Year one, almost nothing changes. Eight billion people, and the only difference is silence in the maternity wards.
After twenty years, the youngest person alive is twenty. Schools close for good. Every job that needs young hands starts to go unfilled.
After forty years, the youngest workers are middle-aged. Farms, hospitals and power plants lose their crews faster than they can be replaced.
By seventy or eighty years, the anthropologist Michael Little estimates, shortages of food, water and medicine have already taken most people.
Very few humans live past a hundred. So within about a century, nobody. After 200,000 years, it ends not with a disaster, but with one quiet birthday.

description:
What if everyone on Earth stopped having children? Binghamton University anthropologist Michael A. Little, writing for The Conversation, estimates that with no new births the species would be gone within about 100 years, since very few people live past a century, and that most people would be gone within 70 to 80 years as food, water and medical care failed.
The decline would start slowly, but once too few young people were left to grow food, run hospitals and care for the old, societies would break down quickly. World population is about 8 billion today, up from 4 billion in 1974, and Homo sapiens has existed for at least 200,000 years.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: The UN still expects world population to peak near 10 billion in the 2080s, so this one stays hypothetical. Who would you want running the last power plant? Drop your own what-if below.
